title: Formulas, Domains, and Ranges of Quadratic-Radical Compositions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = 1 - sqrt(x). (a) Write formulas for f o g and g o f, and find the (b) domain and (c) range of each composite function.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } (f \circ g)(x) = (1 - \sqrt{x})^2,\ (g \circ f)(x) = 1 - |x|;\quad \text{(b) } D_{f\circ g} = [0, \infty),\ D_{g\circ f} = (-\infty, \infty);\quad \text{(c) } R_{f\circ g} = [0, \infty),\ R_{g\circ f} = (-\infty, 1]

steps.title: Write the Composite Formulas in Part (a)
steps.explanation: Substitute g(x) = 1 - sqrt(x) into f(x) = x^2 to get (1 - sqrt(x))^2. Substitute f(x) = x^2 into g(x) = 1 - sqrt(x) and use sqrt(x^2) = |x| to get 1 - |x|.
steps.why: For all real x, the principal square root of x^2 simplifies to |x|.

steps.title: Find the Domains of f o g and g o f in Part (b)
steps.explanation: For f o g, the inner function g(x) = 1 - sqrt(x) requires x >= 0, and f(u) = u^2 accepts all real inputs, so D_{f o g} = [0, infinity). For g o f, f(x) = x^2 is defined for all real x and always satisfies x^2 >= 0, which lies in the domain [0, infinity) of g, so D_{g o f} = (-infinity, infinity).
steps.why: Since x^2 >= 0 for every real number x, no input is excluded by the outer square root in g(f(x)).

steps.title: Determine the Ranges of f o g and g o f in Part (c)
steps.explanation: For f o g: as x varies over [0, infinity), 1 - sqrt(x) takes all values in (-infinity, 1], which includes 0 (at x = 1) and all negative real numbers; squaring (-infinity, 1] covers [0, infinity). For g o f: since |x| takes all values in [0, infinity), 1 - |x| takes all values in (-infinity, 1].
steps.why: Because (-infinity, 1] contains [0, 1] and (-infinity, 0], its image under squaring is [0, infinity).
